% note: Format flag: yes means the pre-registered format-compliance flag fires for that setting and shape. Its rule, in the file's words: ``non-compliance above 5\% of answered tries''; non-compliance is the share of answered samples (the file's ``tries'') whose format was not ok, one minus the format compliance (checked). Refusals, truncations and missing calls are counted apart in the Study~1b file (not in this table) and do not enter the flag: the answered samples leave them out (checked).
% note: Two cells sit at exactly 5.0\% and are not flagged, as the rule says `more than 5\%'.
% note: Pooled accuracy is each puzzle's mean over its two shapes. Intervals are cluster bootstrap over puzzles for settings with several samples and Clopper--Pearson for one-sample settings (the interval type the file records for each setting, in the Interval type column that opens the table's second part); per-shape intervals are of the same type.
% note: Haiku-max's and Opus-medium's intervals here at the lengths of Tests~B1--B3 and those in ⟦TAB-11⟧ (Tests~B1--B3 by shape) come from separate bootstrap draws over the same puzzles, with the same points, and differ only by resampling, so their ends can differ slightly; where both collapsed to one value, both show the same exact interval.
% note: ``(exact, post hoc; \ldots{} puzzles)'' marks a bootstrap interval that collapsed to one value (every puzzle right, or every one wrong), replaced by the exact two-sided 95\% Clopper--Pearson interval from free analysis 4 (post hoc; it changes no test). The count in the mark is the number of puzzles, not of samples (the conservative unit).
% note: Token limit and the trial round's largest output are recorded only for the settings whose limit the trial round set; the Study~1b file records no limit for the other settings, so those cells are empty.
